briefing.headline: Kestrel's high press kept creating turnovers but Harbour punished central exposures and extended the lead

first_half.text: Kestrel pressed aggressively and generated more high regains than Harbour, but those turnovers were not converted into goals while Harbour exploited the centre to score twice.
Harbour concentrated play through the centre and carried more possession into Kestrel’s final third, creating the higher expected goals that produced their lead.

changes.text: Kestrel eased their press after the break — their PPDA rose by 20% — while their defensive line stayed high, conceding more centre entries to Harbour.
Harbour shifted more of the game into Kestrel’s right and the opponent’s final third, increasing final-third entries and possession higher up the pitch.

predictions.text: Gregor Molina would have Kestrel sit slightly deeper to reduce Harbour’s centre entries by at least 30%, but centre entries rose instead.
Kestrel’s PPDA rose by 20% as they eased press intensity, matching the prediction.
Kestrel did not increase final-third entries by 20%—their entries rose only marginally.
Harbour did not raise progressive passing by 15%; the increase fell short of the target.
Harbour moved more into the final third, with final-third entries rising well over 20%.

result.text: Harbour turned sustained final-third pressure into one more goal after the break to finish 3-0, aided by increased centre penetration and possession higher up the pitch.
Kestrel’s reduction in pressing intensity (higher PPDA) and failure to increase final-third entries meant they created no second-half goals despite similar shot counts.
